content:
Apple has shared more details about the Apple Music AI labeling requirements, which were first announced earlier this year in March. Here's what you can expect.

AI-generated content will be clearly labeled on Apple Music

Apple previously announced earlier this year that Apple Music will require AI transparency disclosures for new cover art, tracks, songs, and music videos uploaded to the platform.

Apple has now shared more details about how this system will work.

Apple said in an email to creators today: "Later this year, we will also display these disclosures to Apple Music listeners in the form of a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple also clarified under what circumstances these disclosures need to be made. The email reads:

Apple Music added that their efforts are aimed at providing listeners with "the greatest possible transparency," and directed creators to refer to their style guide for more information.

Apple Music's move is just the latest example of a streaming platform responding to the surge of AI-generated music, as more and more musicians incorporate generative AI into their production processes.

Spotify previously said it would remove AI character music from editorial picks and algorithmic recommendations by default; Deezer also announced last year that tracks fully generated by AI would not appear in their recommendations and editorial playlists. Deezer went even further last month, disclosing that music fully generated by AI accounts for over 50% of their daily uploads—a first.

As for Apple Music, platform head Oliver Schusser previously revealed on Billboard's On the Record Podcast that although more than one-third of the music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of streams on the platform.
